title: Notification pods restarting
summary: notification-service pods began OOMKilling at 07:52 UTC after a deploy at 07:12 UTC introduced an unbounded per‑locale template cache. GC overhead warnings appeared from 07:35 UTC, memory utilization climbed to the 1 GiB limit, and consumer lag and error rates rose as a consequence of repeated restarts. No other config, flag, secret, or infra changes occurred in the window.

hypothesis.mechanism: Unbounded per‑locale template cache introduced in v3.9.2 retains entries indefinitely, causing steady heap growth, high GC overhead, and eventual OOMKill.
predictions: Heap dump shows cache objects dominate retained heap
A cache‑size metric would show monotonic increase

hypothesis.mechanism: Higher request rate pushes normal memory usage over the 1 GiB limit.
Kafka consumer lag forces the service to buffer large batches, exhausting memory.
The 1 GiB memory limit is insufficient for current workload even without a leak.

facts.statement: GC overhead high warnings (~35‑37%) appear continuously from 07:35 UTC.
First OOMKill recorded at 07:52:13 UTC; total 27 OOMKill events until 08:29 UTC.
Memory utilization climbed from baseline 0.55 to peak 1.00 (1 GiB limit) with mean 0.82.
Consumer lag grew from baseline ~129 messages to last 41,370 messages.
Request rate increased ~10% from baseline 103 rps to mean 113 rps.
CPU utilization remained near baseline (0.33 to 0.35).
Only production change was deploy of notification-service v3.9.2 at 07:12:30 UTC (commit 0f6c3a8) adding per‑locale template cache.

assumptions.statement: The new per‑locale template cache retains entries indefinitely (no eviction/TTL).
assumptions.reason: Code change adds cache but no bound was mentioned in the diff.

assumptions.statement: Memory usage scales roughly linearly with request rate when cache size is bounded.
assumptions.reason: Typical JVM heap behavior for stateless services.

assumptions.statement: Consumer processes messages in batches whose size is proportional to lag.
The 1 GiB container memory limit has not been altered recently.
assumptions.reason: No infra change recorded for the service.

gaps.reason: Tool cannot retrieve heap dumps; needed to confirm cache domination.
Metric not emitted; would directly show unbounded growth.
No record of consumer config changes; needed to rule out H3.

actions.description: Rollback notification-service to v3.9.1 or disable the new per‑locale cache via feature flag.
actions.rationale: Stops further memory growth immediately; the deploy is the only recent change.

actions.description: Temporarily raise pod memory limit to 2 GiB and add restart‑rate alert.
actions.rationale: Provides breathing room while the fix is validated; prevents immediate OOMKill cascades.

actions.description: Implement bounded cache (LRU/TTL, max entries) and ship hot‑fix v3.9.3.
actions.rationale: Eliminates the unbounded growth root cause.

actions.description: Add cache‑size metric (template_cache_entries) and GC pause time metric.
Obtain heap dump from a restarted pod to confirm cache objects dominate retained heap.
actions.rationale: Closes Gap G1 and validates hypothesis H1.

open_questions: How many distinct locales were seen during the incident?
Does the new cache have any eviction/TTL logic that was inadvertently disabled?
Were there any feature‑flag changes not captured in the change‑history feed?
What is the Kafka consumer `max.poll.records` setting?
